title: Capability
description: Something the company must be able to do, with a declared chain of who does it. Every capability names a primary owner, an ordered fallback chain, and a final fallback that can never itself be absent. A company can lose people, agents, and whole modules without losing a capability: the chain says who picks it up and how much of it survives.

criticality.description: How badly the company degrades if this capability is unavailable. 'high' and 'critical' require at least one intermediate fallback.

fallback.description: Ordered chain tried when the primary is absent, saturated, or stalled. First match wins.

finalFallback.description: The holder that always answers. Typically a human role, because a chain that terminates in an agent can terminate in nothing.

sla.description: The response commitment for the capability as a whole, e.g. 'first response within 4 business hours'.

requires.description: Other capabilities this one depends on. Cycles are permitted (a company is a cyclic graph) but are reported by the capability map.

measuredBy.description: Metrics that show whether the capability is actually being delivered.

Holder.description: One link in the ownership chain. `delivers` is the honest statement of how much of the capability this holder actually provides.

delivers.description: 'full' means no loss. 'reduced' means a documented subset. 'manual' means the automation is gone but the outcome still happens. 'triage-only' means the holder can hold the line, not close the loop.
